questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall the courses were filled to the brim with highschool-esque deadlines consisting of short papers that no one would read, comment or grade. Superficial group work and 5-minute presentations. All things that distracted from the ability to study in depth, when enrolled in 5 different courses. The academic level was low, but the work load was surprisingly high.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level at the faculty of political science was all in all disapointingly low. Analytical approaches were often substituted completely for trivia knowledge. Generally one would spent a huge amount of time studying irrelevant details of specific institutions/countries instead of practicing analysis or applaying theoretical explanations. The classes were mostly tidious and uninspiring, several professors seemed totally laizzes faire in their approach to lectures, with no coherent structure between readings and the subject matter in class. The one subject i attended at the faculty of sociology had a substantially higher skill ceiling, even though the barrier of entry were just as low. It outperformed all courses at the
pol.sci
faculty in terms of academic level, didactics, presentation, structure, coherence.

Política Comparada

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Organizations offers almost no relevant insight for students of political science, except for some specific insights into the UN. The Political Systems in the Maghreb is a very interesting course, but once again is void of theory or comparative analysis. Sistema politico y juridico de la UE is without any coherence whatsoever, and is not recommendable for non-native speakers. Contemporary Sociological Theory is a great course for students of political science who has already studied classical sociology. Politica comparada is a fine entry level comparative politics course.
